cards.front: What personal number does every Washington license, permit and ID card carry?
cards.back: Every Washington license, permit and ID card carries a personal Washington number that often starts with the letters WDL.

cards.front: What is License Express, and whose account must a new driver use?
cards.back: License Express is the secure DOL website, and each new driver must open an account in their own name because services cannot be obtained through someone else's account.

cards.front: When do you count as a Washington resident?
cards.back: You count as a Washington resident when any single listed condition applies, such as keeping a home here for personal use, being registered to vote here, filing taxes with a Washington address, or receiving state public assistance.

cards.front: How long does a licensed adult newcomer have to get a Washington license?
cards.back: A new resident aged eighteen or older who is licensed in another state has thirty days to get a Washington driver license.

cards.front: What must a new resident with an expired out-of-state license pass?
cards.back: If a new resident's out-of-state license has expired, they must pass both the knowledge exam and the skills exam before Washington will license them.

cards.front: What does a licensed newcomer under eighteen apply for?
cards.back: A new resident under eighteen with another state's license applies for a Washington Intermediate Driver License, and DOL must approve their driver education and confirm at least six months of instruction-permit time.

cards.front: How do adult and under-eighteen newcomers differ?
cards.back: A licensed adult newcomer gets thirty days to switch to a Washington license, while a newcomer under eighteen must enter the intermediate license system instead.

cards.front: Is REAL ID a card, and where will a standard license stop working?
cards.back: REAL ID is a law rather than a card, and an enhanced license or ID is one of several options that satisfy it; a standard license will no longer be accepted at airport security, border crossings or secure federal buildings.

cards.front: What must you already have before applying for an instruction permit?
cards.back: You must already have a WDL number before you apply for an instruction permit.

cards.front: How young can you get a permit when enrolled in driver training, and when do you apply?
cards.back: When you enroll in driver training you may apply for a permit as young as fifteen, online or at an office, from one to ten days before the course starts.

cards.front: How do you get a permit without driver training, and when may you take the skills exam?
cards.back: Without driver training you may take the knowledge exam after turning fifteen and a half and get the permit once you pass, but the skills exam and license must wait until you are eighteen.

cards.front: How long is an instruction permit valid, and how long does a passing knowledge score last?
cards.back: An instruction permit is valid for one year and can be renewed for a fee, while a passing knowledge exam score stays valid for two years.

cards.front: How do the permit ages differ with and without a driver training course?
cards.back: The permit age with a driver training course is fifteen, while the permit age through the knowledge exam without a course is fifteen and a half, so the course path starts half a year sooner.

cards.front: Which lasts longer, the permit or the knowledge exam score?
cards.back: The permit itself lasts one year, but the knowledge exam score lasts two years, so the two expiry periods must not be swapped.

cards.front: What must you have done to get a first license at sixteen or seventeen?
cards.back: To get a first license at sixteen or seventeen you must have held the permit for at least six months, be at least sixteen, live in Washington, and complete a traffic safety course at an approved driver training school.

cards.front: When does an out-of-state traffic safety course count in Washington?
cards.back: A traffic safety course finished in another state counts only if it meets Washington's minimum of thirty classroom hours and six behind-the-wheel hours.

cards.front: How many practice hours must a teen log, and with what kind of supervisor?
cards.back: A teen applicant must log at least forty hours of daytime and ten hours of nighttime driving beside a licensed driver with three or more years of experience, attested by a parent, guardian or responsible adult.

cards.front: What driving record must a teen have before applying?
cards.back: A teen applicant must go six months with no traffic violations or convictions before applying, and must have no alcohol or drug offenses while driving on the permit.

cards.front: What does the parent or guardian certify on the in-person authorization form?
cards.back: For an in-person teen application a parent or guardian signs an authorization form certifying at least fifty hours of driving experience and no traffic infractions or violations during the previous six months.

cards.front: How much experience must a teen's supervising driver have?
cards.back: A teen's supervising driver needs three or more years of experience for the practice hours, which differs from the adult permit route.

cards.front: How do the daytime and nighttime practice hours relate to the certified total?
cards.back: The forty daytime plus ten nighttime practice hours add up to the fifty hours that the parent or guardian certifies on the authorization form.

cards.front: How quickly must the driver training school record a teen's exam scores?
cards.back: Once a teen passes each exam, the driver training school has twenty-four hours to record the scores in the DOL system.

cards.front: What does an in-person applicant leave the office with?
cards.back: An in-person applicant leaves the office with a temporary license good for forty-five days, and the official card arrives later by mail.

cards.front: What serves as the temporary license when a teen finishes online, and what can it not do?
cards.back: When a teen completes the license online, the printed receipt is the temporary license, but it carries no photo and so cannot serve as identification.

cards.front: How do the in-person and online temporary licenses differ?
cards.back: The in-person temporary license lasts forty-five days, while the online receipt also acts as a temporary license but cannot be used as identification because it has no photo.

cards.front: What are the four routes for an adult first-time applicant?
cards.back: An adult first-time applicant has four routes: transfer another state's license, pass both exams, pass the knowledge exam and practice on a permit beside a licensed driver with five or more years of experience before the skills exam, or use an exam waiver to get a permit and finish a training course before both exams.

cards.front: How much experience must the supervising driver have on the adult permit route?
cards.back: On the adult route that uses a permit, the supervising licensed driver must have five or more years of experience, longer than the teen requirement.

cards.front: What happens if your vision screening shows you need glasses or contacts?
cards.back: DOL screens your vision before issuing a license, and if you need glasses or contacts that requirement is noted on the license, so wear them every time you drive.

cards.front: What do you need to drive a motorcycle or a commercial motor vehicle?
cards.back: Driving a motorcycle or a commercial motor vehicle requires an extra endorsement added to your personal driver license.

cards.front: Which two restricted phases do sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds pass through?
cards.back: Drivers aged sixteen and seventeen move through two restricted phases, first the instruction permit and then the intermediate driver license, before they hold an unrestricted license.

cards.front: Who may ride with you in the first six months of an intermediate license?
cards.back: In the first six months of an intermediate license you may not carry any passenger under age twenty unless that person is an immediate family member.

cards.front: How many young non-family passengers are allowed after the first six months?
cards.back: After those first six months, and until you turn eighteen or reach one year on the license, whichever is first, you may carry no more than three passengers under age twenty who are not immediate family.

cards.front: When may an intermediate driver not drive, and who can ride along to allow it?
cards.back: An intermediate driver may not drive from one a.m. to five a.m. unless a parent, guardian or licensed driver aged at least twenty-five rides along, and this night limit ends after one year of safe driving.

cards.front: May an intermediate driver use a phone hands-free?
cards.back: Intermediate license holders may not use a cell phone or wireless device while driving, even hands-free, except to report an emergency.

cards.front: How do the two intermediate passenger phases differ?
cards.back: In the first six months of an intermediate license no passenger under twenty is allowed except immediate family, whereas afterwards up to three such passengers are allowed.

cards.front: What different questions do the ages twenty and twenty-five answer?
cards.back: The passenger limit age is under twenty, but the night-hours escort must be a parent, guardian or licensed driver at least twenty-five, so the two ages answer different questions.

cards.front: What happens after a first, second and third intermediate violation?
cards.back: For an intermediate driver, a first violation or at-fault collision keeps the current restrictions until age eighteen, a second brings a six-month suspension or suspension until eighteen if that comes sooner, and a third suspends the license until eighteen.

cards.front: How does a second intermediate violation differ from a third?
cards.back: A second intermediate violation brings a six-month suspension or suspension until eighteen, whichever ends first, while a third suspends the license all the way to eighteen.

cards.front: When may an intermediate driver drive at any hour with passengers?
cards.back: An intermediate driver may drive at any hour with passengers when the trip is for agricultural purposes, or after one year with no crash and no traffic offense.

cards.front: What happens to intermediate restrictions at eighteen?
cards.back: Intermediate restrictions drop away automatically at eighteen, so no new license is required then, and an updated card can wait until renewal.

cards.front: Who receives an early warning letter, and why?
cards.back: DOL mails an early warning letter to drivers aged eighteen to twenty-one after their first moving violation, because a driver's crash risk doubles after that first violation.

cards.front: What does an agricultural permit allow, and what is the juvenile permit's minimum age?
cards.back: An agricultural permit lets a driver under eighteen drive within a set area for farm work, and the juvenile agricultural permit has no minimum age.

cards.front: Can an agricultural permit replace an instruction permit?
cards.back: An agricultural permit never substitutes for an instruction permit and does not waive any requirement for a first Washington license, including practice driving.

cards.front: How does an agricultural permit differ from an instruction permit?
cards.back: An agricultural permit allows farm-work driving in a set area with no minimum age, but unlike the instruction permit it does not count toward a first license.

recap_hooks.text: Your WDL number is personal, your License Express account must be your own, and one listed condition makes you a resident.
Licensed adult newcomers switch within thirty days, an expired license means both exams, and newcomers under eighteen enter the intermediate system.
REAL ID is a law, not a card.
Get your WDL number first; the training path allows a permit at fifteen, the exam-only path at fifteen and a half.
The permit lasts one year and the passing exam score two.
A teen needs six months on the permit, an approved course, forty day and ten night hours, and six clean months.
The parent form certifies fifty hours, and a teen's supervisor needs three years of experience.
Scores are recorded within twenty-four hours, the paper license lasts forty-five days, and an online receipt is not ID.
Adults can transfer, test, practice on a permit with a five-year driver, or use a waiver and a course.
Wear required lenses every drive, and add an endorsement for a motorcycle or commercial vehicle.
Teens go from permit to intermediate license before full privileges.
No young non-family passengers for six months, then up to three.
No driving from one to five a.m. without a qualifying escort, and no phone even hands-free.
A first violation keeps the limits, a second suspends, a third suspends to eighteen.
Farm trips and a clean year lift the limits, they end at eighteen, and young adults get a warning letter after a first violation.
An agricultural permit covers farm work in a set area and never replaces an instruction permit.
